title: Derive the Quadratic Formula
purpose: Symbolic-math fixture for semantic equation transitions, branch preservation, worked-example verification, narration, and accessible formula output.

learner.audience: Secondary or first-year college learners comfortable with algebraic fractions.

objectives.statement: Derive the quadratic formula by completing the square without dropping a branch.
criteria: Adds the same square term to both sides

objectives.statement: Apply and verify the formula for 2x²−7x+3=0.

sources.title: Deriving the quadratic formula by completing the square
sources.creator: Alystria fixture authors

scenes.title: Start with a nonzero leading coefficient
scenes.narration: Begin with a x squared plus b x plus c equals zero, with a not equal to zero, so dividing by a is valid.
scenes.visualIntent: The condition a≠0 is pinned beside the equation and remains visible.
scenes.accessibilityDescription: The general quadratic equation and nonzero condition are read before any transformation.

scenes.title: Complete the square
scenes.narration: Divide, move the constant, and add b squared over four a squared to both sides. The left becomes one perfect square.
scenes.visualIntent: Semantic terms preserve identity while moving; reduced-motion mode uses discrete equations.
scenes.accessibilityDescription: Five numbered equation rows expose each legal transformation in reading order.

scenes.title: Keep both square-root branches
scenes.narration: Taking a square root creates both a positive and a negative branch. Isolating x gives the familiar formula.
scenes.visualIntent: One equation branches into plus and minus paths, then recombines with a ± symbol.
scenes.captionText: Square root step ⇒ both + and − branches
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A branching diagram lists the positive and negative square-root cases explicitly.

scenes.title: Verify two roots
scenes.narration: For two x squared minus seven x plus three, the discriminant is twenty-five. The two roots are three and one half, and both make the original polynomial zero.
scenes.visualIntent: The discriminant calculation feeds two substitution cards with exact rational arithmetic.
scenes.accessibilityDescription: Two labeled substitution rows each simplify the polynomial to zero.

qualityAssertions.description: Every displayed transformation is symbolically equivalent under a≠0.
The square-root step preserves both solution branches.
Exact symbolic substitution verifies both roots.
Equations have semantic text and a transformation reading order.
Formulae fit all targets without scale below the legibility floor.

provenance.notes: All derivation text is locally authored and intended for exact symbolic verification.
